- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3% relative to model output.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true peak observed.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 5+ consecutive days, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.0) or when recent history shows downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% if sentiment is low or flat.
